timeline.label: Filed FY2025 10-K: production 2,375 MBOED, revenue $58.9B, OCF $19.8B, long-term debt $22.4B
Issued senior notes via 424B5 shelf — refreshes debt maturity profile
Closed Marathon Oil acquisition — expanded Lower 48 scale and reserve base
Filed FY2024 10-K: revenue $54.7B; integration reporting post-Marathon
424B5 debt offering — continued investment-grade market access
Historical context: ConocoPhillips separated downstream into Phillips 66 (2012); remains pure-play E&P
S-3ASR shelf registration — standing debt issuance capacity

industry.structure: Global upstream oil and gas is fragmented among majors, large independents (ConocoPhillips, EOG, Devon), and NOCs. Independent E&Ps compete on basin quality, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet discipline; OPEC+ supply policy sets the marginal price floor/ceiling.
industry.share_shift: U.S. Lower 48 shale consolidated through mergers (COP/Marathon, Exxon/Pioneer). Independents with multi-basin portfolios and low breakevens are gaining share versus higher-cost international barrels when prices soften.
industry.trend: Capital return (buybacks, variable dividends) has replaced growth-at-all-costs; LNG export and data-center power demand are new demand vectors, while energy transition policy keeps long-cycle project timing uncertain.
